requirement: BOEM/BSEE issued the rule 30 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 285 (now called 30 CFR 585), which provides a framework for approval of offshore wind turbines.
scope: Offshore wind turbines in federal waters

requirement: USACE retains primary federal jurisdiction for approving offshore wind facilities in the Great Lakes and state waters.
scope: Offshore wind turbines in state waters and the Great Lakes
source: Rivers and Harbors Act of 1899 (Section 10) and Clean Water Act of 1977 (Section 404)

requirement: Developers of planned offshore wind projects in state waters, as well as of advanced projects in federal waters, are likely among the first to need and employ design standards that are relevant to these projects' specific environmental conditions.
scope: Offshore wind turbines in state and federal waters

requirement: Unique design conditions that will have to be addressed for projects in state waters include freshwater ice (Great Lakes), earthquakes (West Coast), significant hurricanes (Gulf of Mexico and Southeast Atlantic coast), tsunamis (Hawaii and Alaska), and large hail (nationwide).
scope: Offshore wind turbines in state waters
